title: When the Harbor Wakes
premise: In the tidal port of San Verrano, 1911, Jude Reyes has survived eleven years of indenture to the Marisol Trading Company by being small, quick, and unremarkable. When a drowned diver surfaces clutching a ledger proving the company has been weighting its pearl contracts with debt-trap clauses, Jude becomes the unwilling courier of evidence that could free every bonded family in the harbor. With the seasonal bridge closed and company enforcers hunting the missing pages, Jude must move the ledger through three checkpoints using the only routes they know: underwater. The journey costs them their invisibility, an ally's life, and finally their indenture papers, burned as a signal fire — but by the last chapter, the magistrate reads the ledger aloud, the contracts are voided, and Jude, no longer anyone's property, chooses to stay in the harbor they once dreamed of escaping.
about_author: Isandro Okafor is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trade ledgers from Southeast Asian and Caribbean ports. Their fiction excavates the lives recorded only as line items, giving names back to the counted.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude Reyes, POV. A day in the life of an indentured diver's child: hauling oyster baskets, memorizing which overseers can be bribed with silence, measuring everything by what fits in two hands. The drowned diver is pulled from the shallows at dusk, a wax-sealed packet strapped beneath his shirt. Emotional beat: the uneasy comfort of routine about to break.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The dead man's widow presses the packet into Jude's hands — pages torn from a company ledger showing divers billed into perpetual debt. She begs Jude to carry it to Magistrate Corvo before the bridge closes. Jude refuses, then finds their own father's name on a debt page. Emotional beat: fear curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Bridge Season
chapters.summary: Company clerk Ambrose Hale, POV. Hale seals the harbor for the monsoon season on Overseer Brannigan's orders, quietly doubling the checkpoint guards. He suspects the missing ledger pages but reports nothing, protecting his own forged signatures within them. Emotional beat: complicity dressed up as prudence.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Jude maps the route: the fish market gate, the customs house, the bridge itself. They recruit Teyo, a smuggler's son who owes Jude's family, to create distractions. First attempt at the market gate fails; Jude hides the ledger inside a hollowed prayer candle. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into craft.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Teyo, POV. Teyo runs the distraction and nearly hangs for it; Jude buys his release by trading a stolen company seal. The two argue — Teyo wants to flee to the outer islands, Jude cannot leave while families remain bonded. Emotional beat: loyalty strained between escape and duty.

chapters.title: Brannigan's Net
chapters.summary: Overseer Brannigan, POV. Brannigan interrogates the widow, burns her stall, and posts a reward that turns neighbors into informants. He suspects Hale's silence and begins squeezing him. The harbor's warmth toward Jude visibly chills. Emotional beat: power revealing how cheaply it purchases people.

chapters.title: Under the Pilings
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. With gates sealed, Jude attempts the route only a diver's child knows: swimming the customs channel at slack tide, ledger wrapped in oilcloth against their chest. Cramped, half-frozen, they surface inside the customs yard — directly into Hale's lantern light. Emotional beat: courage at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale catches Jude but sees his own forgeries in the ledger's margins. In one long night he must choose: turn Jude over and stay safe, or let the child go and burn his career. He unlocks the yard gate and hands Jude his own testimony page. Emotional beat: a corrupt man's first clean act.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. At the bridge checkpoint, cornered with dawn coming, Jude burns their own indenture papers in a brazier to create smoke and chaos, slipping through as guards scatter — Teyo's final diversion costing him a broken arm. Jude reaches Magistrate Corvo's door as the first ferry of the season crosses. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: When the Harbor Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Corvo reads the ledger aloud in the market square; contracts are voided, Brannigan arrested, Hale testifies and loses everything but his name's honesty. The widow reopens her stall; Teyo recovers; Jude stands at the reopened bridge — and turns back toward the water. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as triumph but as a town learning to breathe.
